issue_context.title: RFC: dfu/boot/mcuboot: consider usage of boootloader/mcuboot code
issue_context.body:
## Introduction

mcuboot.c file implements functionality required for interact with MCUBoot bootloader.
This had been introduced before the west was introduced.

Some parts of this code are reimpregnations of what is implemented in mcuboot repository.
Mcuboot's repository provide implementation of function required for application for interact with the MCUboot.

### Problem description

As some code are defined here and there it becomes problem when module is compiled within MCUboot.
It is possible to mitigate problem using #fdefry - but this is temporary hack.
comments: Do you consider to make common the FLASH_* definitions so that the macros that are enabling "image" access don't get redefined all over the code?

I think it makes sense to have much of the definition here in a single place, probably making sense to have it in the mcuboot repo. It mostly makes sense to build this dfu/boot/mcuboot module when mcuboot itself is also being included, so it shouldn't be an issue of the module being present.

review_comments:
There is a missing `#else`. It should be:
```
#error "definition incompatible"
#endif
#else
```

I have noticed that it is not distinguished between failure to access the flag and the flag not being set.
This is not issue to this PR but maybe we need return some other type than bool to distinguish between failures and actual flag check.
Reworking this would be an API change - so, yes not in this PR.

This is a bit confusing to me, you're writing to the correct location but you're writing 4 bytes (`uint32_t`) instead of the usual 8 bytes that MCUboot uses for a flag, and even if it works (with the 0x01 at the right place) it will only work for one specific endianness.

I believe this test-sute entirely written like that (assues 32 bits write access and lite-endianes).
I can rework it to be more widely, but see this as another PR.
Is that Ok for you?
It is acceptable, but I don't see why not just fixing it properly since it's two lines of change.

The only place where `BOOT_SWAP_TYPE_` are needed (but are not provided by MCUBOOT_BOOTUTIL) is mcumgr port. We don't need to do it in this PR, but IMO mcumgr should link to MCUBOOT_BOOTUTIL cmake target to get those macros. After doing so, BOOT_SWAP_TYPE_ macros could be thrown away from this header. This is the last duplicated code from mcuboot I guess.
I prefer to do that in another PR.

`BOOT_MAGIC_SZ` is not needed anymore.

`BOOT_MAX_ALIGN` as well. The only place where you need it is unit test that you have updated. I think MCUBOOT_BOOTUTIL could be linked to unit test to provide that symbol.

both definition are needed in mcumgr and dfu/img_utill/flash_img.c under BOOT_TRAILER_IMG_STATUS_OFFS macro.

As you mention these definition can be removed once that code will be linked with MCUBOOT_BOOTUTIL.
